ὑπέμενον θλίψεις καὶ ἐκπέσωσι τῆς σωτηρίας. 2 Kor 2,15–16 Οἱ εἰδωλολάτραι ἐν
θανάτῳ ὄντες τῷ νοητῷ διὰ τὴν οὖσαν ἐν αὐτοῖς ἀγνωσίαν καὶ πώρωσιν, καὶ
δευτέρῳ περιπίπτουσι θανάτῳ μὴ παραδεχόμενοι τὸ εὐαγγελικὸν κήρυγμα· οἱ δὲ διὰ
τῆς νομικῆς παιδεύσεως πρὸς τὰς ἀρχὰς ἐλθόντες τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ θεοῦ, γεγόνασι
μέν πως ἐν ζωῇ, ὅμως ἐὰν πιστεύσωσι τῷ Χριστῷ, παραδέχονται τὴν ὀσμὴν τῆς
γνώσεως τοῦ πατρὸς ἐκ ζωῆς εἰς ζωήν. Μετ' ὀλίγα ἄλλως ἑρμηνεύει τὴν περικοπὴν
ταύτην. Τὰ τοιαῦτα κατορθοῦντο Χριστοῦ εἶναι εὐωδία, οὐ τῶν τυχόντων ἀλλὰ τῶν
γησίως δουλευόντων τῷ θεῷ. καὶ ὡς φορτικὰ μὲν οὐ λέγει ταῦτα περὶ ἑαυτοῦ, ἐξ ὧν
δὲ ἐπάγων λέγει οὐ γάρ ἐσμεν ὡς οἱ πολλοί, ἐπέδειξεν ἑαυτόν. 2 Kor 2,17
Καπηλεύεσθαι λέγει τὸν λόγον ἤτοι παραμιγνύμενον περιτομῇ καὶ τηρήσει
σαββάτων ἢ διὰ τὸ πορισμὸν νομίζειν τινὰς τὴν εὐσέβειαν. λέγω δὲ ὅτι ἐξ
εἰλικρινείας φθέγγομαι, καὶ αὐτὸ τοῦτο ἐκ θεοῦ ἔχειν φησί, καὶ οὐκ ἀπὸ οἰκείας
δυνάμεως. λέγει δὲ καὶ ἄλλην διάνοιαν, ὅτι διὰ τοῦτο ἐξ εἰλικρινείας, ἐπειδὴ ἐκ θεοῦ
λαλοῦμεν, οὐ παίζοντες τὰ πράγματα ἀλλὰ θεοῦ ἀποκάλυψιν κηρύττοντες. Τοῦτο
λέγει, ἐπειδὴ ἦσαν καὶ ψευδαπόστολοι πορισμὸν ἡγούμενοι τὸν περὶ τῆς εὐσεβείας
λόγον. εἶτα ἐπάγει ἐξ εἰλικρινείας, ἀντὶ τοῦ οὐ παίζομεν φησί τὰ πράγματα, ἀλλὰ
τὴν ἐκ θεοῦ ἀποκάλυψιν κηρύττομεν οὐ καπηλεύοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ.
καπηλεύεται δὲ ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ παραμιγνύμενος περιτομῇ καὶ σαββάτῳ καὶ ἐν τῷ
νομίζειν πορισμὸν εἶναι τὴν εὐσέβειαν. 284 2 Kor 3,1 Ἐντεῦθεν θέλει δεῖξαι ὅσον ὁ
νόμος τῆς χάριτος ἀπολιμπάνεται, ἵνα μή τινες τῶν ἐκ περιτομῆς τῷ ἀξιώματι
Μωϋσέως καὶ τῶν προφητῶν δυσωποῦντες τοὺς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰς τὴν τοῦ νόμου
μετενέγκωσι τήρησιν. 2 Kor 3,2–3 Τοῦτ' ἔστιν αὕτη ὑμῶν ἡ πίστις καὶ ὁ βίος
ἐπιστολὴ πᾶσι γίνεται καὶ γνώρισμα τοῦ ἡμετέρου κηρύγματος. ἐγγεγραμμένη δὲ
πνεύματι, λέγει, τῇ ἐνεργείᾳ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου. διὰ δὲ τοῦ εἰπεῖν πλαξὶ
λιθίναις καὶ καρδίαις σαρκίναις τὴν ὑπεροχὴν τῆς χάριτος πρὸς τὸν νόμον
δείκνυσιν, ὅσῳ καρδία τῆς ἀψύχου πλακὸς κρείττω. δείκνυσι δὲ καὶ ὅσον ἡ χάρις τοῦ
πνεύματος ἀμείνω τοῦ νόμου καὶ τῆς διακονίας τῶν προφητῶν τὸ κήρυγμα τῶν
ἀποστόλων ἀνώτερον. 2 Kor 3,5 Ἀφ' ἑαυτῶν ἀντὶ τοῦ ἀπ' ἀλλήλων. 2 Kor 3,6
Γράμμα λέγει τὸν νόμον, πνεῦμα δὲ τὴν χάριν· ὁ γὰρ νόμος προστάσσων μέν, οὐ
βοηθῶν δέ, βαρεῖ καὶ θανατοῖ διὰ τῆς κολάσεως τοὺς μὴ δυνηθέντας αὐτὸν
πληρῶσαι, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα καθαρὸν ἀπὸ ἁμαρτίας ποιοῦν καὶ παρέχον τὰ χαρίσματα
δηλονότι πρὸς ζωὴν ὁδηγεῖ. 2 Kor 3,7–9 Καὶ μὴν οὐκ ἐν πλαξὶν ἐγένετο ἡ δόξα ἀλλ'
ἐν προσώπῳ Μωϋσέως ὡς ἑξῆς αὐτός φησιν· διὰ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ τὴν
καταργουμένην. ἀλλ' οὐ βουλόμενος πρὸς τὸν προφήτην Μωϋσέα εἰπεῖν, τὸν νόμον
καλεῖ Μωϋσέα, καὶ πρὸς τοῦτον ποιεῖται τὸν λόγον δεικνὺς ἐλάττονα τὴν δοθεῖσαν
τῷ Μωϋσεῖ χάριν τῆς ἀποστολικῆς χάριτος. Εἰ δὲ ἡ διακονία τοῦ θανάτου. Μωϋσέα
λέγει διακονίαν θα285 νάτου, θάνατον καλῶν τὸν νόμον, ἐπειδὴ θάνατον
προεξένησε παρακουσθείς. ἀλλ' οὐκ ἀπὸ τούτου διαβέβληται ὁ νόμος· λέγονται γὰρ
καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι ὀσμὴ θανάτου εἰς θάνατον. ∆ιακονίαν δὲ πνεύματος λέγει τοὺς
ἀποστόλους, καὶ διακονίαν θανάτου τὸν Μωϋσέα. ἀλλὰ φειδόμενος Μωϋσέως
πλακῶν μέμνηται· Μωϋσῆς πλάκας κατήγαγεν ἐξ ὄρους, ἀπόστολοι πνεῦμα τῷ
κόσμῳ ἀποσταλέντες ἐκόμισαν. 284,ξολ2 Καὶ μὴν οὐκ ἐν πλαξὶν ἐγένετο ἡ δόξα ἀλλ'
ἐν προσώπῳ Μωϋσέως. καὶ βουλόμενος ὧδε καὶ πρὸς τὸν Μωϋσέα εἰπεῖν, διὰ τοῦ
νόμου τὸν Μωϋσέα παραδηλοῖ. αὐτὸν δὲ τὸν νόμον διάκονον θανάτου λέγει, ἐπειδὴ
ἐθανάτου ὁ νόμος τοὺς μὴ πληροῦντας αὐτόν. καὶ οὐχ ὡς διαβάλλων αὐτὸν τοῦτό
φησιν, καὶ γὰρ καὶ τοὺς ἀποστόλους ὀσμὴν θανάτου εἶπεν διὰ τοὺς μὴ ὑπακούοντας
τῷ κηρύγματι. ὀσμὴ δὲ θα285,ξολ2 νάτου ἡ περὶ γεέννης ἀπειλὴ αἰώνιον ἐπάγουσα
τοῖς ἀπίστοις θάνατον, καὶ ὀσμὴ ζωῆς τὸ κήρυγμα τῆς βασιλείας εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον
διαπέμπον τοὺς ἑπομένους τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ. ἡ δὲ ὀσμὴ πρόδρομός ἐστιν τοῦ
πράγματος. ∆ιάκονον κατακρίσεως καὶ θανάτου λέγει Μωϋσέα– κατέκρινε γὰρ ἐν τῷ
νόμῳ τοὺς μὴ ὑπακούοντας–καὶ διακονίαν πνεύματος τοὺς ἀποστόλους· Μωϋσῆς
γὰρ τὸν νόμον κατήνεγκεν, οἱ δὲ ἀπόστολοι τὸ πνεύμα τῷ κόσμῳ διεκόμισαν. 2 Kor
3,10 Τὸ δεδοξασμένον τοῦ νόμου γράμμα ἀνεξεταζόμενον πρὸς τὴν ὑπερβάλλουσαν
δόξαν τοῦ πνεύματος οὐ δεδόξασται. οὐδ' ἂν εἴποι τις δεδοξάσθαι ἐν τούτῳ τῷ λόγῳ
pass_a_gloss:
[Continues the 2:14 note: "...for he feared lest they give way on account of the] afflictions which they were enduring, and fall away from salvation.
[Label 2 Cor 2:15-16.] The idolaters, being in the death perceived by the mind on account of the ignorance and hardening that is in them, also fall into a second death, not accepting the gospel preaching; but those who through the training of the law came to the beginnings of the knowledge of God have come to be, in a way, in life; yet if they believe in Christ, they accept the fragrance of the knowledge of the Father from life to life. A little later he interprets this passage otherwise: Those accomplishing such things [the Greek has the corrupt form κατορθοῦντο, read as κατορθοῦντα] are a sweet smell of Christ, not of ordinary people but of those genuinely serving God. And as burdensome things he does not say these about himself; but from the things he adds, saying "for we are not as the many," he showed himself.
[Label 2 Cor 2:17.] He says the word is peddled either being mixed with circumcision and keeping of sabbaths, or through some thinking godliness to be a means of gain. "And I say that I speak out of sincerity": and he says he has this very thing from God, and not from his own power. And he says also another meaning: that for this reason out of sincerity, since we speak from God, not playing with the matters but preaching a revelation of God.
[A second form of the same note, not marked. New material:] He says this, since there were also false apostles considering the word about godliness a means of gain. [The rest repeats: then he adds "out of sincerity," in place of "we do not play with the matters, but we preach the revelation from God, not peddling the word of God"; and the word of God is peddled being mixed with circumcision and sabbath, and in thinking godliness to be a means of gain.] [Page number 284 dropped.]
[Label 2 Cor 3:1.] From here he wants to show how much the law is left behind by grace, so that none of those from the circumcision, putting to shame those from the nations with the dignity of Moses and of the prophets, might transfer them to the keeping of the law.
[Label 2 Cor 3:2-3.] That is: this faith and life of yours becomes a letter to all and a mark of recognition of our preaching. "Written by the Spirit," he says, by the working of the Holy Spirit. And through saying "stone tablets" and "fleshly hearts," he shows the superiority of grace toward the law, by as much as a heart is better than a lifeless tablet. And he shows also how much the grace of the Spirit is better than the law, and the preaching of the apostles higher than the ministry of the prophets.
[Label 2 Cor 3:5.] "From ourselves" in place of "from one another."
[Label 2 Cor 3:6.] He calls the law letter, and grace spirit; for the law, commanding but not helping, weighs down and kills through the punishment those who were not able to fulfill it, but the Spirit, making clean from sin and supplying the gifts, clearly leads toward life.
[Label 2 Cor 3:7-9.] And yet the glory came to be not on the tablets but on the face of Moses, as he himself says next: "on account of the glory of his face, which was being done away." But not wishing to speak against the prophet Moses, he calls Moses the law, and makes his speech toward this, showing the grace given to Moses to be less than the apostolic grace. "But if the ministry of death": he calls Moses a ministry of death, calling the law death, since, having been disobeyed, it procured death. But the law is not slandered from this; for the apostles too are called "a smell of death to death." And he calls the apostles a ministry of the Spirit, and Moses a ministry of death. But sparing Moses he makes mention of tablets: Moses brought tablets down from a mountain; apostles, sent to the world, brought the Spirit. [Page number 285 dropped.]
[Second catena form, marked 284 col. 2 and 285 col. 2. Repeats: and yet the glory came to be not on tablets but on the face of Moses; and wishing here also to speak against Moses, through "the law" he hints at Moses; he calls the law itself a minister of death, since the law put to death those not fulfilling it; and not as slandering it does he say this. New material:] for he also called the apostles a smell of death on account of those not obeying the preaching. And a smell of death is the threat about Gehenna, bringing eternal death on the unbelieving, and a smell of life is the preaching of the kingdom, sending on to eternal life those following the teaching. And the smell is a forerunner of the thing. He calls Moses a minister of condemnation and of death, for he condemned in the law those not obeying. [Repeats: and a ministry of the Spirit the apostles; for Moses brought down the law, but the apostles carried the Spirit to the world.]
[Label 2 Cor 3:10.] The glorified letter of the law, being examined against the surpassing glory of the Spirit, has not been glorified. Nor would anyone say it has been glorified in this account ... [continues in the next section: "of the comparison toward what surpasses"]
pass_b_english: … afflictions they were enduring, and fall away from salvation.

On 2 Corinthians 2:15–16: The idolaters are in a death of the mind because of the ignorance and hardness within them, and when they do not accept the preaching of the gospel they fall into a second death as well. But those whom the training of the law brought to the beginnings of the knowledge of God are, in a sense, already in life; yet if they believe in Christ, they receive the fragrance of the knowledge of the Father, from life to life. A little later he explains this passage differently: Those who achieve such things are the fragrance of Christ, and they are not just anyone, but those who serve God sincerely. Since such words would sound boastful, Paul does not say them of himself; but by what he adds, “For we are not like the many,” he pointed to himself.

On 2 Corinthians 2:17: By “peddling” the word he means either mixing it with circumcision and sabbath-keeping, or the way some people treat godliness as a way to make money. “I say that I speak out of sincerity”: and he says he has this very sincerity from God, not from any power of his own. He also gives another sense: we speak out of sincerity because we speak from God, not trifling with these matters but preaching a revelation from God.
The second catena form adds: He says this because there were also false apostles who counted the word about godliness a way to make money.

On 2 Corinthians 3:1: From here on he wants to show how far the law falls short of grace, so that no one from the circumcision would use the standing of Moses and the prophets to shame those from the Gentiles into keeping the law.

On 2 Corinthians 3:2–3: That is, this faith and life of yours becomes a letter to everyone and a token by which our preaching is known. “Written with the Spirit,” he says, meaning by the working of the Holy Spirit. By saying “tablets of stone” and “hearts of flesh,” he shows how far grace surpasses the law: as far as a heart is better than a lifeless tablet. He also shows how much better the grace of the Spirit is than the law, and how much higher the preaching of the apostles stands than the ministry of the prophets.
On 2 Corinthians 3:5: “From ourselves” stands for “from one another.”

On 2 Corinthians 3:6: He calls the law “letter” and grace “spirit.” The law gives commands but no help, and so it weighs down those who could not fulfill it and kills them by its punishment. The Spirit cleanses from sin and supplies the gifts, and so it plainly leads to life.

On 2 Corinthians 3:7–9: And yet the glory was not on the tablets but on Moses' face, as he says next: “because of the glory of his face, which was being done away.” Not wanting to speak against the prophet Moses, he calls Moses “the law” and aims his words at it, showing that the grace given to Moses is less than the grace of the apostles. “But if the ministry of death”: he calls Moses a ministry of death, and calls the law death, because the law, once disobeyed, brought death about. Yet this does not discredit the law, for the apostles too are called “the fragrance of death to death” (2 Corinthians 2:16). He calls the apostles a ministry of the Spirit and Moses a ministry of death. But to spare Moses he speaks of tablets: Moses brought tablets down from the mountain, while the apostles, sent into the world, brought the Spirit.

The second catena form adds: He called the apostles a fragrance of death because of those who do not obey the preaching. The fragrance of death is the threat of Gehenna, which brings eternal death on unbelievers; the fragrance of life is the preaching of the kingdom, which sends those who follow the teaching on to eternal life. A fragrance runs ahead of the thing itself. He calls Moses a minister of condemnation and of death, for in the law he condemned those who did not obey.
On 2 Corinthians 3:10: When the glorified letter of the law is weighed against the surpassing glory of the Spirit, it has not been glorified. No one would say it has been glorified in this matter …
notes: 2026-11-11 claude-sumfix-b3: retranslated from the locked Greek. The old English was a word-order gloss, printed the 2:17 and 3:7-9 notes twice, and garbled 3:5 ('Higher than the apostles, from themselves rather than from one another'). Doublets collapsed: 2:17 (first form kept; second form's sentence on false apostles printed under 'The second catena form adds:'); 3:7-9 (first form kept; the 284/285 col. 2 form's new sentences printed the same way; it reads 'wishing' where the first reads 'not wishing' to speak against Moses). Corrupt κατορθοῦντο and γησίως read as κατορθοῦντα, γνησίως. The 2:15-16 note also stands under Cyril (cyril-fragmenta-2-corinthios u02-open); kept here because this Greek has it. Labels one per note (2:15 to 3:10); page numbers 284, 285 dropped; section opens and ends mid-sentence with '…'.
